title: Every app opening re-sends up to a year of workouts to the gym's trainers, though the rule says once every 6 hours
what: With sharing with trainers switched on, the app is meant to send on opening at most once every 6 hours. The time of the last send is kept only while the app is running, so each fresh opening counts as 'never sent'. Each time, the phone reads up to a year of sets plus the member's whole older history for best weights, and uploads up to about 280 KB. The gym mates share and the leaderboard push forget their wait the same way. Android closes apps often, so on a slow 4G phone most openings pay for this in data and battery.
expected: The last send time is saved on the phone, so a fresh opening within 6 hours sends nothing; a saved workout still sends at once.
who: members who share with trainers or gym mates
fix_line: Save the time of the last send on the phone so the 6-hour wait survives closing the app

title: Each member who leaves makes the database read the busy-machines records of every gym
what: When a member leaves, a clean-up deletes their busy-machine records by member alone. That list is only indexed by gym first, so the delete reads the list for every gym. Removing a member for good does the same on the record of which gym messages they have seen. The database's own advisor flags both. It is small today and grows with every gym.
expected: Each list has an index on the member, so a leave touches only that member's rows.
who: every gym, as the platform grows
fix_line: Add an index on the member for the busy-machines list and the messages-seen list
